subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements (FinServCorp)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finservcorp.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements (FinServCorp)

Hi Alex & Priya,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier — appreciate the time. Per our call, wanted to summarize the key pain points, success criteria, and next steps so we’re all aligned. If I missed anything, let me know.

Summary of your pain points and goals:
- PII handling: must ensure sensitive customer data (SSNs, account numbers, payment info) is never stored in cleartext or used to train models.
- Retention requirements: logs and request payloads need to be retained for audit but also purged according to your regulatory retention windows (30/90/365 day tiers depending on data class).
- Audit logging & provenance: you need immutable audit trails for inference requests, including requester identity, model/version, inputs (redacted as needed), output hashes, and timestamps.
- Redaction: automated redaction at the request-level for high-risk fields, plus ability to supply custom redaction rules.
- Access controls: RBAC and KMS integration mandatory; SSO (Okta) compatibility.

Current stack you shared:
- AWS (VPC), primary data store: Snowflake; identity via Okta; SIEM: Splunk

Success criteria for a pilot (as discussed):
1) No PII leaves your VPC in cleartext; proof via architecture and short-run tests.
2) Ability to configure and enforce retention windows (30/90/365d) with scheduled purge + auditability.
3) Demonstrate audit logs with required fields (requester, model, model_version, request_hash, timestamp) exported to your Splunk instance.
4) Redaction policy working on a sample set (we'll validate on example payloads).

Immediate next steps and owners:
- Marissa (Redwood): Share SOC2 attestation and our security checklist (attached) — by EOD 11/18.
- Rishi (Redwood infra): Prepare a short architecture diagram and notes on how we handle KV cache and PII isolation for private deployments — by 11/20.
- FinServ (Alex/Priya): Send 2-3 representative example requests (sanitized or masked) and confirm the retention class mapping you expect for each — by 11/20.
- Schedule a follow-up technical review w/ your security team (suggestional slot: Tue 11/23 10:00am PT).

Attachments: Redwood-Security-Checklist.pdf (summary), RW-SOC2-Attestation.pdf (cert).

If that all looks right, I’ll queue the architecture diagram and propose the calendar invite for the technical review.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0112

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finservcorp.com>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finservcorp.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements (FinServCorp)

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few things and a couple of quick clarifying Qs: 

1) Retention windows: primarily looking at 90 days for request payloads, 365 days for audit logs, and 30 days for transient debug logs. We’ll validate these against legal but that’s our default.
2) Redaction: we can provide sample payloads but need the redaction stage to be demonstrable (i.e., before logs are persisted anywhere). Is redaction performed client-side (before sending) or at the inference gateway in your private deployment?
3) Audit log export to Splunk: yes, that’s critical — can you confirm log schema and whether logs can be pushed to our Splunk ingest endpoint?

We’ll prepare 3 sample requests (sanitized) and loop in our security lead if needed for the technical review. Tue 11/23 10am PT works on our side.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product, ML
FinServCorp
alex.johnson@finservcorp.com | (212) 555-0147

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements (FinServCorp)

Looping in Vivek with a couple quick notes on implementation and items we should prep for the technical review: 

- Redaction: For our private (VPC) deployments we typically perform redaction in the inference gateway layer prior to writing any persistent logs. That gives us deterministic redaction and keeps the KV cache free of sensitive spans. We can also support customer-supplied regex rules and a plugin for structured PII detectors.
- Retention: We support configurable retention policies per-log-stream. For audit logs we ship immutable entries (append-only) and we can configure export to customer Splunk via HEC with TLS + token. We’ll need the Splunk endpoint and token for final testing.
- SOC2 attestation: attached (already sent by Marissa) — for the review we should have a short slide (1-2) that summarizes our log schema (fields: timestamp, request_id, user_id(masked), model, model_version, request_hash, redaction_flags).

Action items for us before Tue 11/23:
- Prepare architecture diagram + short slide of log schema (Vivek).
- Sample redaction demo using a pseudo payload and our detector (Rishi).

Rishi
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
